quick_skim.title: Cyclotron: A Recurrence Language for Expressing Interprocessor Communication
quick_skim.abstract: We present Cyclotron, a compiler that expresses streaming dataflow algorithms using recurrence equations, which are then compiled to distributed topologies of interlinked processors. Our compiler lowers a language of recurrences over logical iteration spaces into per-processor programs of sends, receives, and computations. In these recurrences, data accesses are not limited to external accesses to memory; data can live separately on the iteration space itself, allowing internal points to communicate values directly with other points. Users specify this communication directly in the recurrence language, which allows them to express various communication patterns such as a nearest-neighbor systolic exchange, a one-to-all broadcast, a bidirectional split ring, or an asymmetric and piecewise broadcast pattern, which are often not supported by standard distributed linear algebra libraries. These recurrences describe the algorithm and communication independently of how they map onto the hardware. A programmer then chooses which dimensions execute across processors and which execute over time, without rewriting the entire program. Users only specify data dependencies across the iteration space, and the compiler safely generates a program, per process, with correct placement of both communication and computational operators according to the chosen space--time mapping. We evaluate distributed matrix multiplication, TRSM, Cholesky, and fused Cholesky--TRSM on up to 16 CPU nodes and 16 GPUs, comparing against ScaLAPACK, SLATE, and cuSolverMp. Cyclotron is competitive with and often outperforms these hand-optimized libraries; for Cholesky, the best communication strategy changes with problem size and architecture.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: Compiler language that expresses interprocessor communication patterns like broadcast and systolic exchange
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 用编译语言表达广播、脉动交换等处理器间通信模式

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Cyclotron compiles recurrence equations over logical iteration spaces into per-processor send/receive/compute programs, letting users express broadcast, systolic exchange and other communication patterns directly.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对在分布式处理器拓扑上手工编写发送、接收与计算程序繁琐的问题，作者提出 Cyclotron 编译器，用递推方程表达流式数据流算法，并把逻辑迭代空间上的递推下降为各处理器的通信与计算程序。数据可直接驻留在迭代空间上，使用户能显式表达最近邻脉动交换、一对多广播与双向通信等模式。该工作将通信模式提升为语言原语，为自动生成分布式通信程序提供了通用方法。

quick_skim.title: TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time-Constrained Federated Learning
quick_skim.abstract: Minimizing the wall-clock time required to reach a target accuracy is crucial in federated learning (FL), where many applications require frequent model updates as data distributions evolve over time. Nevertheless, in heterogeneous environments, slow clients with limited computational and communication capabilities can delay global synchronization, forcing faster clients to wait and increasing the overall training time. To mitigate this straggler effect, recent studies have introduced per-round time constraints and adapted client workloads within the available time. However, these approaches primarily focus on local computation, whereas communication can become a major bottleneck in communication-limited environments, motivating the joint optimization of training workload and communication compression. Although previous studies have explored such joint optimization, determining an effective training--communication balance under a fixed per-round time budget remains challenging, as the resulting model performance depends on both training progress and compression-induced degradation. We therefore propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes the local training workload and communication compression under per-round time constraints. TALLOP predicts the training loss achievable under different computation budgets from the early-stage mini-batch loss trajectory (LENS), and estimates the degradation caused by communication compression using a compression-error model (CLEN). TALLOP combines these predictions to select the training-communication allocation that minimizes the post-compression loss under the given round time constraint. Experiments in heterogeneous FL environments show that TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time-to-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, although the benefit over training-only adaptation depends on the setting.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: joint optimization of local computation and communication compression under per-round time constraints
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 每轮时间约束下联合优化本地计算与通信压缩

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Proposes TALLOP to jointly optimize local training workload and communication compression in time-constrained federated learning, mitigating stragglers and communication bottlenecks.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对联邦学习异构环境中慢客户端拖慢同步、通信可能成为瓶颈的问题，本文提出TALLOP，在每轮时间约束下联合优化本地训练量与通信压缩策略。方法不再只关注本地计算，而是把通信压缩纳入统一的时间约束优化，以缓解掉队者效应并缩短达到目标精度所需的墙钟时间。该框架面向通信受限场景，强调计算与通信的联合调度，其联合优化视角对LLM分布式训练中的计算通信协同亦有借鉴意义。

quick_skim.title: SigmaTrace: Library-Agnostic Observability for CPU/GPU-Initiated RDMA Communication
quick_skim.abstract: RDMA networking enables low-latency, high-bandwidth communication on large systems. Despite its adoption, however, observability is lacking. Existing tools target specific communication libraries or only report aggregated data, missing per-operation behavior. The gap is widest for GPU-initiated networking, whose in-kernel RDMA operations are invisible to the host.   We present SigmaTrace, a library-agnostic RDMA profiling framework providing fine-grained, per-operation visibility for CPU and GPU-initiated networking. It traces operations at the libibverbs/mlx5dv layers, the common denominator beneath communication libraries on InfiniBand and RoCE, and employs a low-overhead memory interposition technique that, to our knowledge, gives the first observability into GPU-initiated RDMA without source patching or binary instrumentation.   Host-side tracing adds 1.3% overhead on NCCL AllReduce at 128 GPUs and under 2% on RCCL at 1024 GPUs. On a persistent-kernel BFS and Mixture-of-Experts inference, SigmaTrace exposes an in-kernel barrier spread and 2.13x inter-node traffic skew invisible to existing profilers.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: library-agnostic RDMA profiling beneath communication libraries enables diagnosing collective communication bottlenecks
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 库无关的RDMA剖析可定位集合通信性能瓶颈

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: SigmaTrace profiles CPU- and GPU-initiated RDMA operations at the libibverbs/mlx5dv layers, giving library-agnostic per-operation visibility via low-overhead memory interposition.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: RDMA网络在大规模系统中广泛使用，但缺乏细粒度可观测性，GPU发起的网络操作对主机不可见。作者提出SigmaTrace，在libibverbs与mlx5dv层面对CPU和GPU发起的RDMA操作做逐操作追踪，并用低开销内存插桩实现库无关的剖析。该工具弥补了现有方案只覆盖特定通信库或仅给出聚合数据的不足，有助于定位集合通信与分布式训练中的通信性能瓶颈。
